XIIII.}}</noinclude>forraine souldiars: so shal there come many towards the end of the world, and make them selues Christes and Authors of Sectes, and shal gaine many Disciples: as in plaine wordes foloweth in this chapter v. 22. ''There shal rise vp False-Christs and False-Prophets &c''.

''14. The abomination of desolation.''] No heresie doth so properly and purposely tend to this abomination of desolation {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Hyppolyt. li. de Antichristo. Cypr. de Coen. Do. nu. 2.''}}* which by Antichrist shal be atchieued, as this {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Caluinisme tendeth to the abomination of desolation.}}Caluinisme: which taketh away with other Sacraments and external worship of God, the very sacrifice of Christes Body and bloud. Which being taken away (as S. Cyprian saith) no religion can remaine.

''22. Signes and Wonders.''] False-Christes and False-Prophets be seducers, who in the later day by the power of the diuel shal seeme to worke wonders, and yet men must not beleeue them. Much lesse these, which for their false faith can not shew so much as one false miracle.

{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text={{sc|The passion}} according to S. Marke in these tvvo chapters, is the Gospel at Masse vpon Tuesday in the Holy Vveeke.}}{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XIIII.}}}}}}

{{c|''Iudas by occasion of Marie Magdalens ointment, doth sel him to the Councel of the Ievves 12 After the Paschal lambe he giueth them the bread of life (Io. 6.) in a mystical sacrifice or separation of his bodie and bloud. 27 and that night, is after his prayer, 43 taken of thee Ievves men, Iudas being their Captaine: is forsaken of the other eleuen for feare: 53 is falsly accused, and impiously condemned of the Ievves Councel, 65 and shamefully abused of them: 66 and thrise denied of Peter. Al euen as the Scriptures and him self had often foretold.''}} {{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=14|verse=1}}}}{{sc|Nd}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=TENEBRÆ Wednesday.}}the Pasche vvas and the Azymes after tvvo daies: and the cheefe Priests and the Scribes sought hovv they might by some vvile lay hands on him, and kil him.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 26, 1. Lu. 22, 1.''}} {{verse|chapter=14|verse=2}}† For they said, Not on the festiual day, lest there might be a tumult of the people.

{{verse|chapter=14|verse=3}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 26, 6. Ioan. 12, 3.''}}* vvhen he vvas at Bethania in the house of Simon the Leper, and sate at meate, there came a vvoman hauing an alabaster boxe of ointment, of pretious spike-narde: and breaking the alabaster-boxe, she povvred it out vpon his head. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=4}}† But there vvere certaine that had indignation vvithin them selues, and said, VVhereto is {{sup|‖}} this vvast of the ointment made? {{verse|chapter=14|verse=5}}† For this ointment might haue been sold for more then three hundred pence, and giuen to the poore. And they murmured against her. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=6}}† But {{sc|Iesvs}} said, {{sup|‖}} Let her alone, vvhy do you molest her? she hath vvrought a good vvorke vpon me. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=7}}† for the poore you haue alvvaies vvith you: and vvhen you vvil, you may doe them good: but {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ We haue not Christ here needing our almes, as when he conuersed vpon the earth. ''See Mat. 26, 11''.}}∷ me you haue not alvvaies. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=8}}† That vvhich she had, she hath done: she hath preuented to anoint my body to the burial. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=9}}† Amen I say to you, VVheresoeuer this Gospel shal be preached in the vvhole vvorld, that also vvhich she hath done, shal be told for a memorie of her.

{{verse|chapter=14|verse=10}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 26, 17. Lu. 22, 7.''}}* Iudas Iscariote one of the Tvvelue vvent his vvay to the cheefe Priests, for to betray him to them. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=11}}† VVho {{hws|hea|hearing}}<noinclude>{{rh|||ring}}</noinclude>
